title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: In January 2023, the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security (MOLESS) promulgated a guideline for municipalities aiming to declare themselves as Child Labour Free Zones (CLFZ). This initiative is a critical component of the Second National Master Plan (2018–2028), developed to eliminate child labour in Nepal. The guideline provides a comprehensive framework outlining the step-by-step process and key benchmarks for municipalities to achieve the status of a child labour-free zone. ILO has been providing support to the MoLESS for implementing the Second National Master Plan on the Elimination of Child Labour for the past 5-10 years. With support from the United Kingdom Foreign and Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO), the ILO provided written technical comments and suggestions on the draft guidelines shared by the MoLESS in January 2022. The recommendations included increasing girls access to school education, creating a well-functioning database of children and children at work, and strengthening child labour monitoring mechanisms at the municipal level, which are well reflected in the guidelines endorsed by the MoLESS. After the adoption of the guidelines by the government, the ILO, with support from the FCDO, has entered into implementation agreements with three municipalities (Pauwadungma Rural Municipality and Bhojpur Municipality in Koshi Province and Panauti Municipality in Bagmati Province) to support their efforts in making their child labour-free zones. The ILO's support includes technical support for conducting baseline surveys and creating a database system; orienting municipal officials on child labour-free zones; training for schoolteachers on child-friendly learning; and orienting workers and employer organisations on international standards on child labour and their responsibilities to make municipalities child labour-free zones.
